reason: The immediate goal is to put the station on reserve, so connecting the charged battery at the shutdown controls seems like a practical first step.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to emergency power or prepare for shutdown, though other actions may also be needed.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so addressing it at the controls also seems important; I chose the reserve power first.
Moving the heat store could protect the garden, but the stated first goal is to put the station on reserve.

effect: The reserve now carries essential loads, but the fuel plant and normal garden circulation are off. The nook has low-power outlets for survival equipment.
reaction: The dimming lights and quiet plant make the storm preparation feel immediate; I’m concerned about the garden’s circulation.
reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so I want to address it at the shutdown controls before moving the garden.
expectation: I expect this to isolate or otherwise protect the water line, though I don’t know exactly what the controls will do.

alternatives.reason: The charged heat store could help protect the beds, but the exposed line also needs attention.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, with its pump and thaw checks on essential power. The next goal is to move both troughs and the heat store into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line makes practical sense when its heating is lost; I’m curious how the garden will manage without normal circulation.
reason: The heat store can provide warmth in the sheltered nook, so I’ll move it in first.
expectation: I expect the charged tank to be placed in the nook, ready to release heat near the troughs.

alternatives.reason: The lettuce also needs shelter, but bringing in the heat store first seems useful.
The potato trough needs shelter too, but I chose to place the heat source first.

effect: The warm tank is in the nook, where it can buffer the first cold hours while reserve power supplies longer-term heat.
reaction: The distinction between stored heat and longer-term heating makes the arrangement clearer.
reason: Both troughs need shelter; I’ll move the lettuce first.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the warmed nook.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs to go in, and either order seems reasonable.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and its common-return couplings are capped for the move. The potato trough still needs to join it.
reaction: Carrying the bed level and protecting the leaves makes the move feel concrete.
reason: The potato trough is the only remaining gameplay option and the goal calls for both beds in the nook.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be moved into the sheltered nook alongside the lettuce and heat store.

effect: Both troughs and the heat store are now in the nook, completing the chapter’s goals. The potato bed keeps its reservoir, root cover, and support during the move.
reaction: I liked the concrete detail of making room for both beds and clearing the potato leaves around the screen.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining and isolating the outdoor water line was the most worthwhile action: it connected the loss of heating to a practical way to protect the water system.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the two troughs separately felt somewhat repetitive, although their different shapes and fittings gave each move some detail.

surprise.text: I had not expected the warm tank to provide only a short buffer while reserve power supplies longer-term heating; that distinction clarified how the nook works.

arbitrary.text: The order of moving the lettuce and potato troughs felt largely arbitrary, though both clearly needed shelter.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the station and garden fare through the storm and what Earth learns from the articulated body.
